In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the most contaminated areas and with the assessment of their spatial extent.
the identification of priority areas for soil assessment and monitoring, which are areas with high concentrations of heavy metals and where soil quality may be threatened.
the spatial distribution of heavy metals in soil, and the assessment of the potential threat to soil resources in the European Union.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a considerable threat to soil resources from heavy metals in Europe, but the threat is not uniform across Europe.
soil contamination by heavy metals is an issue of concern in the EU and the proposed areas for further investigation and monitoring are the most affected ones.
the soil quality in the majority of European soils is good, but the threat of contamination with heavy metals in some regions and in some cases in large areas is significant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the majority of the European soils is in good condition, but there are still areas where local assessment of heavy metal pollution is suggested.
the majority of the EU land area is not affected by soil contamination by heavy metals, however, there is a considerable proportion (1.2 Mkm(2)) of the EU land that is potentially affected.
